title: Architecture skills assessment
body:
# Architecture skills assessment — T9 TOGAF ADM capability (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

## Categories

The assessment covers the seven categories of the Architecture Skills Framework in SPEC_V2 §8.1: general; business skills and methods; architecture skills; programme and project management; general IT knowledge; technical IT skills; and legal environment. Each is assessed at a proficiency level per role, against the role's job key, with a date and evidence; `crates/api/tests/architecture_capability.rs::a_skills_assessment_names_its_role` proves that the seven categories and the job key are required.

## Proficiency by role

No proficiency is asserted by this rework. P0's `skills-assessment` document (SA-1), delivered by #122's A7, is the proposed baseline and states proposed for P0 acceptance (plan §2); it is not a measured `architecture_skill_assessment` row, and this pass did not run `architecture.skills_assess`. Naming a proficiency for the programme architect, the Board or any delivery role without a dated assessment would invent a receipt. The instrument is live; the measurement is the capability owner's dated activity.

## Baseline

With no measured row, the baseline is P0's proposed SA-1 content. The plan's starting-state table records that no skills row existed at the build; the first adopted assessment becomes the baseline the next review compares against. The retrospective record keeps that distinction explicit rather than treating a proposal as evidence.

## Development milestones

The development plan is the set of milestones a tranche review can hold the capability to, one per category and role where a gap is measured. No milestone row is claimed here because no assessment was adopted. When the Board records the assessment, the milestones become dated targets; until then the `architecture.skills_assess` action and its test are the proof that the shape is enforced, not that a result exists.
